acceptance: The operator's choice between protecting ship-pack scanners as a class and file-by-file entries is recorded in docs/architecture/packages/internal-guards.md with its reason
If the class option is chosen, a test fails when a whole-tree scanner in a repocontract.Packages() package is not covered by guards.ProtectedSurfaceManifest
fix: Operator decision first: either (a) protect ship-pack scanners as a class, for example by deriving manifest coverage from repocontract.Packages() for the scanner test files and adding a predicate that fails when a pack package's whole-tree test is not covered, or (b) keep file-by-file entries and record the rule for when a scanner earns one. Then implement the chosen option red first, with the manifest change landed through an operator-gated evolve ship --class manual.
summary: The inbox rank P2 review protected one scanner, go/internal/inboxrank/weightsort_ban_test.go (the one-ranking guard), by a file entry in guards.ProtectedSurfaceManifest at the operator's approval. Every package in repocontract.Packages() runs at each ship and several hold whole-tree scanners of the same nature (sizeratchet, rawgitratchet, repocontract's own detectors, testmainexit, acssuite's tag guard, the inbox-writer force scan in cmd/evolve outside the pack). Today a scanner is protected only if its file name is gate-shaped (contains guard or ends _gate.go) or an operator adds a file entry, so a lane can weaken an ungated scanner it touches.
title: Decide whether every ship-pack scanner test is a protected surface, as a class, not file by file
